findings.claim: Removing the `done` check means a prematurely closed/ended stream no longer produces the explicit `Stream closed unexpectedly` error; instead `value` is `undefined` and the array destructuring throws an opaque `TypeError: undefined is not iterable`.
findings.rationale: `ReadableStreamDefaultReader.read()` resolves with `{ done: true, value: undefined }` when the stream ends. Line 557 destructures `value` unconditionally, so when the producer closes the stream (network drop, aborted request, malformed payload) the consumer now surfaces a confusing TypeError instead of the intentional domain error, and any caller matching on that message will break. Also, if the reject branch relied on the guaranteed-present chunk, downstream promise rejection semantics change. High confidence this is a real behavior regression unless the caller guarantees the stream can never close here — which is exactly what the removed guard was defending against.

findings.claim: `value as PromiseChunk` is now an unsound cast: without the `done` guard, `value`'s actual type includes `undefined`.
findings.rationale: Previously the `if (done) throw` narrowed `value` to the non-undefined branch before the cast, so the assertion was safe. After the change the cast silently launders `undefined` into `PromiseChunk`, defeating the type checker at the exact spot where the runtime failure occurs. Medium-high confidence; depends on how the reader's read() result is typed in this codebase.
